generation.explanation: For a quadratic ax² + bx + c, the roots come from the quadratic formula, and the quantity under the square root — the discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac — controls everything. If Δ > 0 the square root is real and nonzero, giving two distinct roots (the parabola crosses the x-axis twice); if Δ = 0 the ± vanishes, giving one repeated root (the parabola is tangent to the axis); if Δ < 0 the square root is imaginary, so there are no real roots (the parabola never touches the axis). Use the sliders for a, b, and c (or the preset buttons) to watch the parabola, the value of Δ, and the root count change together.
